title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

title: Telegram’s Pavel Durov responds to Russia’s terrorism designation
summary: The Telegram founder said Russia designated him a terrorist after he refused government demands for mass surveillance and censorship on the messaging platform.

title: Senator Schumer proposes agency to address corruption, including Trump’s crypto ventures
summary: The proposed legislation referenced Donald Trump’s disclosure of billions of dollars in crypto earnings in 2025, as well as his family’s business ties to foreign governments.

title: Aviva Investors launches tokenized fund after Central Bank of Ireland approval
summary: The new XRPL-based share class gives eligible investors blockchain-based access to a regulated US dollar liquidity fund while keeping traditional custody arrangements.

title: Canadian crypto ownership increases to 25%: Ontario survey
summary: A survey of more than 2,000 Canadians in late 2025 and early 2026 showed an increasing awareness of risk around the crypto industry and higher ownership of assets.

title: Bitcoin stable as Fed fave PCE inflation sees first monthly drop in six years
summary: Bitcoin and US stocks enjoyed a relief bounce as the South Korea semiconductor rout eased and US PCE inflation data conforms to year-on-year expectations.

title: Hyperscale Data sells 100 BTC to fund Michigan AI data center
summary: The Bitcoin miner is using part of its treasury and a BTC-backed credit facility to fund an AI campus tied to a potential multi-billion-dollar infrastructure contract.

title: Tokenized gold passes DeFi stress test, but less than 2% is used as collateral
summary: A RedStone report found tokenized bullion held up during gold’s sharp sell-off, but DeFi lending adoption remains limited despite surging market growth and trading volumes.

title: South Korean crypto trading surges amid stock market plunge
summary: South Korean crypto exchanges saw a fresh spike in trading activity as the country’s stock market had several days of significant downside.

title: BitRiver founder charged in Russia over alleged $8M fraud
summary: Russian authorities charged BitRiver founder Igor Runets with alleged fraud tied to a $8 million crypto mining equipment deal involving Russian billionaire Oleg Deripaska.
